title: You’re God’s Temple
excerpt: As God’s child, you’re always in His presence because the Holy Spirit lives in you.
scripture: Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?
prayer: Thank you, heavenly Father, for making me your home. You’re alive and at work in me. Everywhere I go, I carry your presence, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
As God’s child, you’re always in His presence because the Holy Spirit lives in you. You don’t have to wait until you’re in church to enjoy Him—you carry His presence everywhere you go. That’s why you can be joyful, calm, and confident every day.

When you were born again, God made your heart His home. Jesus said the Holy Spirit would live in you forever (John 14:16–17). This means you’re never alone—God is with you at home, in school, and everywhere.

So always remember who you are. Live with joy, boldness, and peace every day.

## Prayer

Thank you, heavenly Father, for making me your home. You’re alive and at work in me. Everywhere I go, I carry your presence, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

## Further Study

2 Corinthians 6:16

title: Christ Lives In You
excerpt: When you received Jesus into your heart, you received everything you need for life and godliness.
scripture: …Christ in you, the hope of glory.
prayer: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for giving me all I need in Christ. I live a glorious and beautiful life every day, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
When you received Jesus into your heart, you received everything you need for life and godliness. Christ in you means God’s life, wisdom, strength, joy, and victory are now in you.

Jesus didn’t give you blessings from far away—He gave you Himself. Because He lives in you, you’re not empty or lacking anything good.

So, don’t speak as if you have nothing. Speak God’s Word with boldness. In Christ, you have peace, health, courage, and all you need to live a joyful and victorious life every day.

## Prayer

Dear heavenly Father, thank you for giving me all I need in Christ. I live a glorious and beautiful life every day, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

## Further Study

Romans 12:2

title: Be Full Of Joy
excerpt: You’re meant to be full of joy at all times. As God’s child, joy is part of your life in Christ—it’s already in you.
scripture: For the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.
prayer: No matter what happens, I’m full of joy. I’m happy, and I live in God’s goodness every day. Hallelujah!
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
You’re meant to be full of joy at all times. As God’s child, joy is part of your life in Christ—it’s already in you. Even when things don’t go the way you expect, don’t give in to sadness or anger; choose joy (James 1:2).

Think about Paul and Silas. They were in prison, yet they sang and praised God because their joy didn’t depend on their situation (Acts 16:25–26).

So let your joy show! Smile, sing, and thank God every day. The more you express joy, the happier you become.

## Confession

No matter what happens, I’m full of joy. I’m happy, and I live in God’s goodness every day. Hallelujah!

## Further Study

title: There Are Treasures In You
excerpt: Did you know there are treasures inside you? Yes!
scripture: …we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellence of the power may be of God and not of us.
prayer: I have treasures in me. I’m full of wisdom and strength. God’s life and glory are at work in me every day. Glory to God!
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
Did you know there are treasures inside you? Yes! As God’s child, He has placed good things in your spirit—wisdom, strength, and the ability to do great things. Jesus said that, “…out of the good treasure of his heart brings forth good things...” (Matthew 12:35). This means you already have what you need to succeed.

How do you bring these good treasures out? By studying, believing, and speaking God’s Word. When you say what God says about you, those good things begin to show in your life.

So always declare, “I’m strong, I’m wise, and I’m blessed!”

## Confession

I have treasures in me. I’m full of wisdom and strength. God’s life and glory are at work in me every day. Glory to God!

excerpt: As God’s child, what makes you different isn’t where you come from or what you have; it’s God’s blessing in your life.
scripture: The blessing of the Lord makes one rich, and He adds no sorrow with it.
prayer: Thank you, precious Father, for blessing me. I’m like a tree planted by the rivers, always growing, succeeding, and producing good results, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
As God’s child, what makes you different isn’t where you come from or what you have; it’s God’s blessing in your life. This blessing helps you succeed and do well.

The Bible says a blessed person is like a tree planted by rivers of water, always growing and bearing fruit (Psalm 1:3). That’s who you are! It means you’ll continue to make progress and produce good results.

So, say it: “I am blessed!” Believe it and walk in it every day. You’ll keep moving from one success to another. Hallelujah!

## Prayer

title: Pray For Others
excerpt: God loves everyone and wants all people to be saved (2 Peter 3:9).
scripture: …pray for one another, that you may be healed. The effective, fervent prayer of a righteous man avails much.
prayer: I’m ready and excited to pray for others and share God’s love. Through me, many children will know Jesus. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
God loves everyone and wants all people to be saved (2 Peter 3:9). That’s why He wants you to pray for others—your friends, classmates, and children around the world.

In the Bible, Elijah stood for God even when others didn’t listen. He encouraged the people to turn back to God (1 Kings 18:21). He didn’t give up.

You can do the same in your own way. Pray for your friends, show them kindness, and tell them about Jesus. As you do this, you’re helping others know God and receive His love.

## Confession

I’m ready and excited to pray for others and share God’s love. Through me, many children will know Jesus. Amen.

Ephesians 6:18

title: You’re God’s Ambassador
excerpt: An ambassador represents their country in another place. In the same way, you represent Jesus here on earth (2 Corinthians 5:20).
scripture: Now then, we are ambassadors for Christ.
prayer: Thank you, precious Father, for making me your representative. Through me, your wisdom, power, and love are seen everywhere I go, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
An ambassador represents their country in another place. In the same way, you represent Jesus here on earth (2 Corinthians 5:20). This means you show God’s love, truth, and power everywhere you go.

When you speak God’s Word and pray, heaven responds. Jesus said that what you declare in line with God’s will is established (Matthew 18:18). That means your words matter.

So, think and act like God’s ambassador. Let your words, actions, and choices show His light and love to others every day.

## Prayer

Isaiah 32:1

title: Your Prayers As Incense
excerpt: Did you know that when you pray, something beautiful happens in heaven? The Bible says your prayers rise up to God like sweet-smelling incense.
scripture: …golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.
prayer: Dear loving Father, you’re worthy of my praise and worship. As I pray and give thanks, my words rise to you as a sweet fragrance, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
Did you know that when you pray, something beautiful happens in heaven? The Bible says your prayers rise up to God like sweet-smelling incense.

In Bible days, priests burned incense as part of worship. Today, your prayers are like that incense before God. When you talk with Him, thank Him, or pray for others, your words rise to Him like a sweet fragrance.

King David understood this when he said, “Let my prayer be set before You as incense…” (Psalm 141:2). God loves to hear your prayers, so keep praying always because He plans to answer. Your prayers are precious to Him.

## Prayer

Dear loving Father, you’re worthy of my praise and worship. As I pray and give thanks, my words rise to you as a sweet fragrance, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

## Further Study

Revelation 8:4

title: God’s Plan
excerpt: God has a special plan for your life. As you study His Word, you learn what He wants you to do.
scripture: And whatever you do, do it heartily, as to the Lord and not to men
prayer: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for your plan for my life. I stay focused on you, and do what you’ve told me to do, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
God has a special plan for your life. As you study His Word, you learn what He wants you to do. But distractions like worries, games, or unimportant things can pull your attention away. That’s why you must stay focused on Him.

Jesus said His goal was to do God’s work and finish it (John 4:34). Paul also kept going, not minding what happened (Philippians 3:13–14). They didn’t give up.

So, be faithful in what God gives you to do. Do it with all your heart. Stay focused, finish well, and please God every day.

## Prayer

Dear heavenly Father, thank you for your plan for my life. I stay focused on you, and do what you’ve told me to do, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

title: Always Prophesy
excerpt: To prophesy means to speak words from God that bring encouragement, strength, and life.
scripture: For you can all prophesy one by one, that all may learn and all may be encouraged.
prayer: Thank you, faithful Father, for your Word in my heart. I speak words that bring life, strength, and encouragement, and I grow in wisdom every day, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
To prophesy means to speak words from God that bring encouragement, strength, and life. When you speak God’s Word, you build others up and help their faith grow.

For example, you can say, “The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want” (Psalm 23:1). When you speak like this, you remind yourself and others that God takes care of you.

The Bible tells us to desire to prophesy so we can bless others (1 Corinthians 14:1). So, speak words of faith over your life— about your health, your academics, and your future. Through God’s Word, you can bring joy and encouragement to everyone around you.

## Prayer

Thank you, faithful Father, for your Word in my heart. I speak words that bring life, strength, and encouragement, and I grow in wisdom every day, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

So choose faith, not fear. Speak God’s Word and act on it. Remember, you’re safe, sound, and victorious every day because God is with you.

title: The Holy Spirit Is With You

series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
The Holy Spirit is your special helper and friend. He lives in you and is always with you. This means you’re never alone!

Jesus went to heaven, but He sent the Holy Spirit to be with us every day. The Holy Spirit helps you know God, teaches you what is right, and gives you power to live the way God wants you to. The apostles did great things because they had the Holy Spirit. He guided them and made them bold.

So, always remember He’s with you: in school, at home, and everywhere. With Him, you can live in joy, do great things, and please God every day.

## Further Study

title: The Name Of Jesus Is Your Authority
titleOriginal: The Name Of Jesus Is Your Authority
excerpt: The Name of Jesus isn’t ordinary— it’s your authority. When you use the Name of Jesus, it’s like Jesus Himself is speaking.
scripture: And whatever you ask in My name, that I will do.
prayer: Dear precious Father, thank you for giving me the authority to use the Name of Jesus. As I live and use the Name, I see changes in and around me, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
The Name of Jesus isn’t ordinary— it’s your authority. When you use the Name of Jesus, it’s like Jesus Himself is speaking. The Bible says God gave Jesus a Name above every name (Philippians 2:9-11). This means everything listens to His Name.

In the Bible, Peter said, “…in the Name of Jesus…rise up and walk,” and the man was healed (Acts 3:6-8). That same power is given to you!

You can use the Name of Jesus when you pray, when you’re faced with a difficult task, or when you need help with anything. Use the Name with faith and boldness, knowing that His Name works. Remember, you have victory through the Name of Jesus every day.

## Prayer

Dear precious Father, thank you for giving me the authority to use the Name of Jesus. As I live and use the Name, I see changes in and around me, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

title: Refuse To Compromise

series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
To compromise means to settle for something or to do something you didn’t plan to do. The Bible says that in the last days, some people will choose to do wrong and ignore God’s Word because others are doing it (2 Timothy 3:1–5). That’s why it’s important for you to always stand for what is right.

Sometimes, others may try to make you follow the crowd or do something you know isn’t good. As God’s child, always stand for what is right. Choose to do His Word, and do what pleases Him.

A good example is Daniel in the Bible. Even when others around him did wrong, he chose to obey God and did not compromise (Daniel 1:8). Like, Daniel, always stand for what is right, and let God’s Word guide your choices.

## Prayer

Dear loving Father, thank you for your Word in me. It guides me in all my choices and decisions. In all I do, I stand for what is right, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
body:
To compromise means to settle for something or to do something you didn’t plan to do. The Bible says that in the last days, some people will choose to do wrong and ignore God’s Word because others are doing it (2 Timothy 3:1–5). That’s why it’s important for you to always stand for what is right.

Sometimes, others may try to make you follow the crowd or do something you know isn’t good. As God’s child, always stand for what is right. Choose to do His Word, and do what pleases Him.

A good example is Daniel in the Bible. Even when others around him did wrong, he chose to obey God and did not compromise (Daniel 1:8). Like, Daniel, always stand for what is right, and let God’s Word guide your choices.

## Prayer

Dear loving Father, thank you for your Word in me. It guides me in all my choices and decisions. In all I do, I stand for what is right, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

message:
Living for the Lord means doing what pleases Him at all times. That means your choices, thoughts, words, and actions are all for Him. When you live this way, you won’t take things too personally or stay angry for long.

The Bible tells us that Samuel became very upset with the children of Israel when they asked for a king (1 Samuel 8:4–7). But God corrected Samuel. The people “…have not rejected you,” the Lord said, “…they have rejected Me.” If anyone was to be upset, it was the Lord, not Samuel.

God helped Samuel understand not to take things personally. In the same way, when someone hurts your feelings, talk to the Lord about it instead of responding in anger. Ask yourself, “Will my reaction please the Lord?” When you live to please the Lord, your heart will stay peaceful at all times.

## Prayer

series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
When Jesus lived on earth, He showed us what true humility looks like. Even though He is the Son of God, He allowed John to baptize Him (Matthew 3:13–15). He didn’t act more important than others. He chose to obey God.

He also told His disciples that anyone who wants to be great must be ready to serve (Matthew 20:26). He even washed their feet to show them how (John 13:13–15).

The Bible says Jesus humbled Himself and did what God wanted. As a result, God lifted Him and gave Him the highest name (Philippians 2:9–11).

So, to be great, you have to choose humility. Choose to do things in God’s way. Help at home. Be kind at school. Stay teachable. Remember, God lifts up the humble.

series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
Kindness is powerful. When someone is unkind to you, it may feel natural to respond the same way. But God teaches us a higher way. The Bible says we should overcome evil with good (Romans 12:21).

Think about what happens when you turn on a light in a dark room; darkness disappears immediately! In the same way, love and kindness are stronger than unkindness. Jesus showed us this by loving people, even when they treated Him badly.

When you choose to forgive, help, and speak kindly, you shine God’s light in a dark world. Your good actions can help others see God’s love. So always choose good, no matter what anyone does to you. You’re God’s shining light, and light always wins.

body:
Kindness is powerful. When someone is unkind to you, it may feel natural to respond the same way. But God teaches us a higher way. The Bible says we should overcome evil with good (Romans 12:21).

Think about what happens when you turn on a light in a dark room; darkness disappears immediately! In the same way, love and kindness are stronger than unkindness. Jesus showed us this by loving people, even when they treated Him badly.

When you choose to forgive, help, and speak kindly, you shine God’s light in a dark world. Your good actions can help others see God’s love. So always choose good, no matter what anyone does to you. You’re God’s shining light, and light always wins.

## Confession

body:
God has given you many wonderful blessings:

peace, joy, victory, and His Word. But God doesn’t

want you to only know about them. He wants you

to enjoy them every day.

In the Bible, there was a man named Caleb.

God promised him a place called Hebron. Even

though giants were living there, Caleb wasn’t

afraid. He trusted God and said, “...the Lord will

be with me...” And He did! Caleb received what

God had promised him (Joshua 14:12-14).

We shouldn’t let fear, doubt, or problems stop

us from enjoying what God has already given us

in Christ. When we trust God, speak His Word,

and stay strong in faith, we can enjoy all His Scan toblessings.

God is with you, and He helps you every step of

the way!

message:

When someone is baptized, it means they’re saying, “I believe in Jesus, and I choose to follow Him.” The Bible teaches us that when we are baptized, we are joined to Jesus and become one with Him.

In the Bible, the Apostle Paul met some people who wanted to better understand baptism. He explained it to them, and they were baptized in the Name of the Lord Jesus (Acts 19:5). This showed that their lives now belonged to Jesus.

When you were baptized, something great took place—you were joined to Jesus, and His Name was proclaimed upon you. You now live in His love and His power. Glory to God!

title: Never Ruled By Fear
excerpt: Some children allow fear to stop them from doing what is right or from trusting God.
scripture: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear…
prayer: I have the Spirit of power, love, and a sound mind; therefore, I have nothing to fear. No matter what happens around me, I always win. Glory to God!
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
Some children allow fear to stop them from doing what is right or from trusting God. They may be afraid of failing an examination or worried about what might happen in the future. But as a child of God, fear has no place in you. The Bible says you have the Spirit of power, love, and a sound mind (2 Timothy 1:7).

Remember Daniel in the Bible? When the king commanded everyone to pray only to him, Daniel wasn’t afraid. He continued praying to God just as he always did. Even when he was thrown into the lions’ den, Daniel trusted God completely—and God delivered him! (Daniel 6:12-23).

So don’t let fear of anything control you. God is with you and lives in you. You’re never alone and never afraid. Hallelujah!

title: Your Prayer Has Power
excerpt: Prayer is not something we do only when we’re in trouble. Prayer is powerful!
scripture: …The effective, fervent prayer of a righteous man avails much.
prayer: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for hearing me when I pray. As I pray in the Name of Jesus, your power works in my life, my family, my school, and my world. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
Prayer is not something we do only when we’re in trouble. Prayer is powerful! When you pray, you’re taking action because God listens to you and responds.

The Bible tells us about Elijah. He prayed to God, and it did not rain for three and a half years. Later, he prayed again, and God sent rain (James 5:17–18). Elijah was not special because he was perfect—his prayers worked because he trusted God and believed His Word.

In the same way, when you pray for your family, your friends, your school, or yourself, God hears you. Pray with faith, speak in the Name of Jesus, and know that God answers your prayers. Your prayer truly has power!

## Prayer

body:
Have you ever wondered what you would do if

Jesus suddenly appeared in front of you? Would

you shout for joy, kneel down, or just stand

amazed? Whatever you do will come from what

is in your heart—your spirit.

Think about Saul, who later became Paul. He

was on his way to hurt Christians when suddenly,

a bright light from heaven shone around him.

He heard Jesus speak, but because his heart was

full of anger and confusion, all he could say was,

“Who are you, Lord?” (Acts 9:5). His response

showed the condition of his spirit at that moment.

That’s why it’s so important to fill your heart with

God’s Word—by reading your Bible, listening to

God’s teachings, and praying in tongues every

day. When God’s Word fills your heart richly,

your spirit becomes trained to hear, recognize, Scan toand respond to God the right way.

## Confession

My heart is full of God’s Word; therefore, I’m always attentive to His voice, and I respond the right way, every time!

That same blessing is at work in you today. It brings health, favour, wisdom, and success. It helps you excel in your studies, your friendships, and everything you do. You are blessed to prosper and blessed to win— always. Hallelujah!

title: You Are The Light
excerpt: God made you wonderfully special and unique—there’s no one else in the whole world exactly like you!
scripture: You are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hidden… Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.

series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
God made you wonderfully special and unique—there’s no one else in the whole world exactly like you! And Jesus said you are the light of the world (Matthew 5:14). What does that mean?

It means your life is meant to shine—to be bright with God’s love, joy, kindness, and excellence so others can see your light.

Think of Joseph. Even when his brothers were unkind to him, even when he became a slave, and even when he was thrown into prison, he didn’t stop shining. Joseph kept trusting God and doing everything with excellence. And soon, God promoted him to become a great leader in Egypt!

Just like Joseph, you can shine wherever you are—at school, at home, in church, or with friends. When you choose to be kind, helpful, joyful, and full of love, your light shines brightly, and people will see your good works and glorify your heavenly Father.

Today, choose to be God’s helping hand by showing love to your friends, family, classmates, and anyone who needs care. Every act of kindness you show is like doing it for Jesus Himself!

excerpt: As God’s child, God has already declared, “You’re forgiven and free from sin!” This is called justification.

message:

This is called justification. It means God sees you as clean, right, and perfect in His eyes. Jesus took your place so you could take His place—standing before God as His special, beloved child.

Before Paul met Jesus, he made wrong choices and even hurt God’s people. But when he met Jesus, his whole life changed! Paul became a transformed person and began preaching boldly about Jesus everywhere (Acts 9:1–22). Paul didn’t earn this new life—God gave it to him as a gift because of what Jesus did.

Now, because of Jesus, you also have a brand new place with God—a place filled with His glory, power, and victory. So, go through your day knowing you stand with Jesus in a place of strength, honour, and greatness. Hallelujah!

title: One Sacrifice Was Enough
excerpt: Before Jesus came, God’s people had to offer animals every year to cover their sins.
scripture: So Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many. To those who eagerly wait for Him He will appear a second time…
prayer: Dear heavenly Father, I thank you for the sacrifice of Jesus Christ on my behalf. Therefore, I’m perfect, righteous, and justified! Hallelujah!
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
Before Jesus came, God’s people had to offer animals every year to cover their sins. But those sacrifices couldn’t make anyone truly clean on the inside. They were only temporary. Something perfect—something that would work forever—was needed.

That’s why Jesus came. He didn’t bring another sacrifice… He was the sacrifice!

The Bible calls Him “...the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world” (John 1:29). Jesus gave His life as the perfect sacrifice once and for all, so your sins could be taken away completely and forever.

Because of Jesus, you never have to feel guilty or ashamed. You don’t need to “fix” yourself or try to earn forgiveness. Jesus already paid the full price—perfectly and forever. Hallelujah!

title: God’s Spirit Is God’s Answer
excerpt: After Peter and John healed the lame man, the leaders warned them never to speak or teach in the Name of Jesus again.
scripture: And when they had prayed… the place… was shaken; and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with boldness.
prayer: The Holy Spirit lives in me; He is God’s answer in my life! He gives me boldness, wisdom, and power to do great things for the Gospel. Hallelujah!
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
After Peter and John healed the lame man, the leaders warned them never to speak or teach in the Name of Jesus again. But instead of being afraid, they gathered with the other disciples and prayed. They asked God for boldness to keep preaching the Gospel.

As they prayed, the whole place shook! But that shaking wasn’t God’s answer. God’s real answer was the Holy Spirit. The Bible says they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and then they spoke God’s Word with boldness (Acts 4:31). Hallelujah!

That’s how God answers you, too. Whatever you ask for—help, courage, or even money—His Spirit gives you wisdom and boldness. Remember when Jesus and Peter needed to pay tax? Jesus knew exactly where the money was—in the mouth of a fish—because the Holy Spirit guided Him (Matthew 17:24–27). God didn’t drop money from the sky; He gave wisdom, and that wisdom brought the answer!

That’s why praying in other tongues and listening to the Holy Spirit are so important. He guides you every day!

title: Present Your Strong Reasons
excerpt: One day, a Roman centurion had a servant who was very sick.
scripture: “Present your case,” says the LORD. “Bring forth your strong reasons,” says the King of Jacob.
prayer: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for always hearing me when I pray. I present your Word as my strong reason, and I pray with confidence, knowing that I receive whatever I ask according to your will, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
One day, a Roman centurion had a servant who was very sick. The centurion believed Jesus could heal him, so he sent some Jewish elders to speak to Jesus on his behalf. At first, Jesus didn’t go with them. But when the elders explained how kind the centurion was—and how he had helped build their synagogue—Jesus went with them immediately (Luke 7:4–6).

The elders presented strong reasons, and this teaches us something powerful about prayer.

When you talk with God, He wants you to present your case using His Word. That means you don’t just pray, “Lord, please help me.” Instead, you pray with reasons from the Bible— God’s promises!

For example, you can say: “Father, your Word says all things work together for good to them that love you (Romans 8:28). I love you, so I declare that everything is working for my good!”

That’s how to pray boldly and confidently—with strong reasons from God’s Word.

title: Carriers Of Covenant Kindness
excerpt: When God blessed Abraham, He wasn’t thinking of just one man—He was thinking of the whole world!
scripture: ...and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying to Abraham, ‘And in your seed all the families of the earth shall be blessed.’

So when you show kindness, forgive quickly, speak lovingly, and help others, you’re spreading God’s covenant kindness. Everywhere you go— school, home, or church—God’s blessings flow through you to lift others and show His love.

title: Love Sees Real Value
excerpt: Some people think love is just a feeling—like saying, “I love my best friend because she’s nice,” or “I love him because he helps me.” But real love…
scripture: He who does not love does not know God, for God is love.
prayer: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for your love that sees beyond what people do or how they look. I choose to love others just like you love me—seeing their true value and treating them with kindness every day, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
Some people think love is just a feeling—like saying, “I love my best friend because she’s nice,” or “I love him because he helps me.” But real love is much more than that. True love isn’t based on how people act or look—it comes from God, because God is love!

When God looked at the world, He saw how valuable people are, even though many didn’t believe in Him or obey Him. The Bible says, “For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son…” (John 3:16). God didn’t love the buildings or the trees—He loved people! Even when they did wrong things, He still saw their true worth and sent Jesus to save them.

That’s the kind of love God has put inside you. It’s called the God-kind of love, and it helps you see others the way He does. So, don’t love people only when they’re kind or friendly. Love everyone— because that’s how God loves you. When you see others through His eyes, you’ll realize that everyone is precious and valuable.

## Prayer

message:

message:

Therefore, walk in the newness of life—free, forgiven, and full of God’s righteousness. Hallelujah!

excerpt: Did you know the Holy Spirit has a name? Yes, He does! “Holy Spirit” isn’t His name—it’s who He is!
scripture: Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
Did you know the Holy Spirit has a name? Yes, He does! “Holy Spirit” isn’t His name—it’s who He is! It’s like calling someone “human being” instead of his real name.

The Holy Spirit answers to the Name of Jesus. That’s why the Bible never tells us to pray to the Holy Spirit or ask Him to do something. Rather, we’re instructed to pray in the Name of Jesus, and the Holy Spirit will get to work. He’s the One who makes the power and presence of Jesus real in our lives.

So, whenever you call on the Name of Jesus, know that the Holy Spirit is at work, bringing His power and glory into the situation to cause a change. Hallelujah!

## Prayer

Dear heavenly Father, thank you for the power in the Name of Jesus. As I use His Name, I see the works of the Holy Spirit in all that concerns me, in Jesus’ Name. 36Amen.

title: You’re Righteous
excerpt: God is righteous; righteousness is His nature. Think about it: God can never be wrong. He’s always just, right, and perfect. That’s why He’s God!
scripture: For if by the one man’s offense death reigned through the one, much more those who receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness will reign in life through the One, Jesus Christ.
prayer: Dear loving Father, thank you, for giving me the gift of righteousness to stand before you without fear or guilt. Therefore, I’m bold and confident every day because your nature is in me. Hallelujah!31
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
God is righteous; righteousness is His nature. Think about it: God can never be wrong. He’s always just, right, and perfect. That’s why He’s God! And you know what’s amazing? You’re just like Him! He gave you His nature of righteousness the moment you were born again. It’s His free gift to all His children.

For example, Abraham was called righteous because he believed God (Genesis 15:6). Righteousness gave him boldness to walk with God and receive His blessings.

That’s what righteousness does for you too— it gives you the confidence to stand before God without fear, guilt, or shame. So, never think or feel unworthy of God’s blessings and goodness because you’re God’s righteousness in Christ Jesus!

## Prayer

title: He’s Your Peace and Grace
excerpt: As God’s child, you’ve been blessed with grace and peace.
scripture: Grace and peace be multiplied to you in the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.
prayer: I’m on top, in charge, and in control of all situations because Christ is in me and He’s my peace. Hallelujah!
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
As God’s child, you’ve been blessed with grace and peace. Grace is God’s power working in you, helping you to be strong, wise, and successful in everything you do. And God’s peace isn’t just a calm feeling— it’s a powerful gift from God.

The Bible calls it perfect peace: peace that comes with safety, health, and prosperity (Isaiah 26:3).

The Lord Jesus was full of God’s grace (John 1:14) and always peaceful, no matter what happened. One day, while a severe storm tossed the boat around, Jesus was sleeping peacefully, completely calm (Luke 8:22–25).

Nothing bothered Him, and He wants you to be like that too—calm, confident, and at peace no matter what happens, knowing that “…the peace of God… will guard your hearts and minds…” (Philippians 4:7).

## Confession

title: Jesus Took Your Place
excerpt: Have you ever swapped seats with a friend? That’s a little like what Jesus did for you—only what the Lord Jesus did was much greater!
scripture: For He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, that we might become the righteousness of God in Him.
prayer: Dear loving Father, thank you for giving me a special place in Christ, a place of joy, victory, and blessing. I live every day knowing you’re with me, and I reign over challenges, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
Have you ever swapped seats with a friend? That’s a little like what Jesus did for you—only what the Lord Jesus did was much greater!

The Bible says He took your place so you could take His place in righteousness. Long before it happened, the prophet Isaiah saw it in a vision: the Son of God would be wounded for our sins, beaten so we could be whole, and by His stripes we are healed (Isaiah 53:4–6).

When He came, everything happened just as God planned. He was judged, beaten, and killed—all for you. His sacrifice made you right with God! Now, you live sin-free and enjoy God’s blessings every day through His resurrection. Glory to God!

## Prayer

title: Study God’s Word
excerpt: God’s Word is full of treasures that can help you live a great life.
scripture: Desire God’s pure word as newborn babies desire milk. Then you will grow in your salvation.
prayer: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for giving me your Word to build me up and nourish me for the life of greatness you’ve planned for me. My mind is renewed right now by the power of your Word, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
God’s Word is full of treasures that can help you live a great life. However, you can only enjoy these treasures if you take the time to study and meditate on God’s Word for yourself.

Timothy is a great example of someone who gave attention to God’s Word. As a young child, he learned the Scriptures from his mother and grandmother. God’s Word helped him grow into a strong and wise young man. Later on, he became a great helper to Apostle Paul and a leader in the church (2 Timothy 3:15).

You can be like Timothy too! So, start today. Set time every day to study God’s Word. The more of God’s Word in you, the more you’ll grow in wisdom, faith, and strength.

## Prayer

Dear heavenly Father, thank you for giving me your Word to build me up and nourish me for the life of greatness you’ve planned for me. My mind is renewed right now by the power of your Word, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

title: God Lifts The Humble
excerpt: Do you remember how David became king? He was the youngest and the least expected to be chosen as king.
scripture: But He gives more grace. Therefore He says: God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.
prayer: I’m loving, kind, and humble. I rejoice at God’s goodness in others. Therefore, I receive more grace to grow, shine, and do excellent things. Hallelujah!
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
Do you remember how David became king? He was the youngest and the least expected to be chosen as king. But God saw something special in him—a humble and gentle spirit. That’s what truly matters to God—your heart!

The Lord loves it when we’re humble and loving. When you’re humble, you don’t look down on others or get upset when they succeed. Rather, you celebrate them and thank God for their blessings.

God lifts you higher and gives you more grace when you walk in humility. So, be kind, be happy for others, and let love shine through everything you do. Remember, God gives more grace to those who are humble.

## Confession

message:

title: Satan Doesn’t Know Your Mind
excerpt: Have you ever played a game where you tried to guess what someone was thinking? No one gets it right until the person says what’s on their mind.
scripture: But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, the hidden wisdom which God ordained before the ages for our glory
prayer: Thank you, precious Father, for giving me victory over the devil and all things. My heart is full of God’s Word, and I walk in strength and triumph each day, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
Have you ever played a game where you tried to guess what someone was thinking? No one gets it right until the person says what’s on their mind.

That’s how it is with the devil. He can’t read your mind—he can only hear what you say. That’s why it’s so important to speak words of faith, not fear. In the Bible, the devil couldn’t harm Job and his family until Job spoke his fears. Job said, “For the thing I greatly feared has come upon me, and what I dreaded has happened to me” (Job 3:25).

So, what should you do? Fill your heart with God’s Word. When your heart is full of His Word, you’ll speak the right words—words of faith, victory, and joy. Remember, “…For out of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaks” (Luke 6:45). That’s how to stay ahead of the devil and live victoriously every day. Hallelujah!

## Prayer

Thank you, precious Father, for giving me victory over the devil and all things. My heart is full of God’s Word, and I walk in strength and triumph each day, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

message:

message:

excerpt: All through the Bible, we read about people who gave to God in faith—and God responded with amazing blessings.
scripture: So let each one give as he purposes in his heart, not grudgingly or of necessity; for God loves a cheerful giver.
prayer: My faith is alive and active! As I give in faith, I become a channel of blessing to my world, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
All through the Bible, we read about people who gave to God in faith—and God responded with amazing blessings.

For example, Solomon once gave God a thousand burnt offerings. That night, God appeared and said, “…Ask! What shall I give you?” (1 Kings 3:5). Solomon could have given just one offering, but he went the extra mile— and God noticed!

Noah also gave a special offering after the flood, and the Bible says that God smelled the sweet aroma and made a promise never to curse the ground again (Genesis 8:21). And our Lord Jesus gave the greatest offering of all—His life! Because of that, God highly exalted Him and gave Him a Name above every name (Philippians 2:9).

When we give to God with faith, love, and joy—whether it’s our time, talents, or offerings— God always responds with blessings. So, give cheerfully, trust Him completely, and always give in faith and with joy.

## Prayer

title: Be Ready For His Return
excerpt: Have you ever had a surprise guest show up at your house? Imagine if your room was messy—you’d feel unprepared and probably rush to clean it up.
scripture: Therefore you also be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.
prayer: I live each day ready for the Lord’s return. I live to please and serve Him, share His love, and tell others about Him every day. Amen!
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:

Some people live as if the Lord is never coming back, but the Bible tells us that He will. One day, Jesus will take with Him all those who believe in Him. This is called “the Rapture”, and it’ll happen suddenly— in a flash! (1 Thessalonians 4:16-17).

So, what should you do? Keep your heart full of love for Jesus. Stay excited about the things of God. Tell others about Him, and live everyday as someone who’s ready to meet the Lord. Don’t just wait—live ready! That’s the best way to prepare for the Lord’s return.

## Confession

title: The Powerful Name Of Jesus
excerpt: Jesus gave us something very powerful— His Name! When you use the Name of Jesus, impossible and hopeless situations are changed.
scripture: …In My name they will cast out demons… they will lay hands on the sick, and they will recover.
prayer: My life is for glory and excellence because I do all things in the Name of Jesus. Therefore, I live victoriously and dominate my world, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
Jesus gave us something very powerful— His Name! When you use the Name of Jesus, impossible and hopeless situations are changed. It’s not about how loud you shout or how strong you feel; what matters is believing in the power of His Name and using the authority it gives.

That’s exactly what Peter and John did when they met a man who couldn’t walk. Peter knew he had something that could change the man’s life. So, he boldly said, “…In the Name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk!” Immediately, the man jumped up, walking and leaping for joy! (Acts 3:6-8).

The Name of Jesus still works today! You can pray for the sick in His Name, and they’ll be healed. You can use His Name to bring peace, victory and change everywhere you go. Hallelujah!

## Confession

My life is for glory and excellence because I do all things in the Name of Jesus. Therefore, I live victoriously and dominate my world, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

message:

Remember, God’s Word is medicine (Proverbs 4:22). So, fill your heart with God’s Word and speak it over your body every day. This is how to stay strong and healthy—both spiritually and physically.

## Confession

title: Dress To Honour God
excerpt: Have you ever dressed up for a special event, maybe your birthday, a wedding ceremony, or church?
scripture: And you shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother, for glory and for beauty.
prayer: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for making me your child, full of beauty and excellence. I choose to live wisely; and when I’m dressed, I bring you honour, showing that I belong to you, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.
series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
Have you ever dressed up for a special event, maybe your birthday, a wedding ceremony, or church? You probably picked your best clothes because you wanted to look your best. The way we dress says a lot about who we are. That’s why God wants us to dress in a way that honours Him.

In the Bible, God told Moses to make special clothes for Aaron, the high priest. These clothes weren’t ordinary; they were made to show God’s glory and beauty. The people who made them were filled with God’s wisdom because those garments were for His service alone (Exodus 28:3).

This teaches us something important: God cares about how we present ourselves. As His children, we should always look neat, clean, and tidy. Our clothes don’t have to be expensive; what matters most is that our appearance reflects God’s excellence and shows that we belong to Him.

## Prayer

Dear heavenly Father, thank you for making me your child, full of beauty and excellence. I choose to live wisely; and when I’m dressed, I bring you honour, showing that I belong to you, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:

Don’t get so busy with schoolwork, games, or chores that you forget what matters most— spending time with God and His Word. The Word of God is your spiritual food and your strength. Just as your body needs food to grow strong, your spirit needs God’s Word to grow too!

The Bible says in Joshua 1:8 that when we study and meditate on God’s Word, we’ll have good success! So, every day, take time to pray, read your Bible, and listen to what God is saying to you. That’s how to live a joyful, peaceful and successful life.

body:
Martha was busy doing many things, but her sister, Mary, sat with Jesus to listen and learn from Him. Jesus commended Mary for choosing the best thing—the Word!

Don’t get so busy with schoolwork, games, or chores that you forget what matters most— spending time with God and His Word. The Word of God is your spiritual food and your strength. Just as your body needs food to grow strong, your spirit needs God’s Word to grow too!

The Bible says in Joshua 1:8 that when we study and meditate on God’s Word, we’ll have good success! So, every day, take time to pray, read your Bible, and listen to what God is saying to you. That’s how to live a joyful, peaceful and successful life.

## Confession

God’s Word is in my heart; therefore, I always win. I walk in peace and victory every day, no matter what happens. Hallelujah!

## Further Study

1 Peter 2:2

series: Rhapsody of Realities for Early Readers
message:
Welcome to a brand-new year! Today is a fresh start to put God first in everything— your time, gifts, ideas, and even your money. Everything we have comes from the Lord, so the best use of it is what matters to Him.

Jesus said, “…Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature” (Mark 16:15). That means we begin this year with God’s priorities: loving Him, helping others know Him, and faithfully serving Him wherever we are— at home, in school, and at church.

When you choose God’s way first— praying, sowing money seed, serving, and sharing the Gospel—He takes care of everything that concerns you. That’s the assurance we have in His Word: “…and it shall be added to you” (Matthew 6:33). What a way to start the year— secure in God’s care!

## Confession

Thank you, Lord, for blessing me with wisdom, and everything I need. This year, I put you first in all I do, using all you’ve given to me to help others know about you. Amen.
